nativeOutcome: One additional household not experiencing very low food security at 12 months
decision: Do not publish a dollars-per-10-QALYs price. The available health-utility estimate describes one adult becoming fully food secure for one year, while the native SFMFB model describes a household crossing only the very-low-food-security threshold. The state transition, person allocation, duration, and organization-specific causal effect are unresolved.

candidateEvidence.design: Longitudinal observational target-trial emulation using nationally representative Medical Expenditure Panel Survey data
candidateEvidence.population: Adults who screened positive for food insecurity; 1,368 were food insecure under the full survey module
candidateEvidence.contrast: Status quo versus a hypothetical intervention making every participant food secure
candidateEvidence.boundary: The estimate is an adult-level one-year health-utility difference for eliminating food insecurity. It is not a randomized intervention effect, a household effect, a very-low-to-low-food-security transition, or evidence about SFMFB Community Markets.

failedGates.label: Match the health-state transition
failedGates.why: USDA classifies both low and very low food security as food insecure. The SFMFB model estimates movement out of very low food security, which may still leave a household food insecure; the candidate utility study estimates becoming food secure.

failedGates.label: Allocate a household outcome to people
failedGates.why: The native result is measured per household, while QALYs accrue to people. No defensible adult/child count, affected-member share, or within-household distribution is available for the modeled Community Market cohort.

failedGates.label: Establish duration
failedGates.why: A 12-month endpoint does not show when the food-security change began, whether it persisted for a full year, or what happened after follow-up.

failedGates.label: Measure the SFMFB causal effect
failedGates.why: The native effect is transferred from Freshplace, which bundled client choice with monthly motivational interviewing and referrals in Hartford. SFMFB has not published a causal Community Market food-security or health-utility result.

illustrativeCounterfactual.assumptions: If, contrary to the missing evidence, every native household outcome meant exactly one adult became fully food secure for exactly one year, use 0.008 QALY per adult-year.
illustrativeCounterfactual.publicationBoundary: This arithmetic is shown only to expose the unsupported assumptions. It must not appear as SFMFB's comparison price, rank, or recommendation.

requiredEvidence: Report the full USDA food-security transition matrix for a defined Community Market cohort, including high, marginal, low, and very low categories.
Report unique household composition and pre-specify which adults and children receive health-utility credit.
Measure SF-6D or another preference-based health utility at baseline and follow-up, with timing sufficient to estimate duration.
Use a credible comparison, complete participant flow, missing-data analysis, and a pre-specified causal estimand.
Publish incremental program cost, public/private displacement, capacity, and a dated marginal funding plan.
